title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction: Short handwritten note on the back of a typescript page (an English translation of a Russian paper on vanishing of H^1 and projective embeddings; unrelated to the note). Grothendieck answers a question from the surrounding notes, probably whether the Galois group of a finite extension L/K_0 acts trivially on an arithmetic invariant. He says this generally fails, even for K_0 = Q, and that a counterexample only needs Z/2Z, i.e. a quadratic field L, acting nontrivially on Pic(A) = Cl(L), where A is the ring of integers of L. He then notes that Z/2Z acts on Pic(A) 'par symétrie', meaning by x ↦ -x (inversion). This holds because for an ideal I, the product I·σ(I) = N(I)A is principal, generated by a rational number. So σ acts as -1 on Cl(L), and the action is nontrivial as soon as Cl(L) is not killed by 2. He concludes that it suffices to find a quadratic field whose class group is not a 2-group, e.g. Q(√-23) with class number 3. The margin note 'demander à Serre ?' shows he meant to check with Serre.
errors: The stated criterion 'Pic(A) not a 2-group' is sufficient but not necessary. The action by inversion is nontrivial exactly when Cl(L) has exponent > 2 (e.g. Cl ≅ Z/4 also works). This is harmless for producing a counterexample.

ideas.what: The nontrivial automorphism of a quadratic field acts on the ideal class group by inversion, because I·σ(I) = N(I) is principal.
ideas.modern_name: Galois action on class groups of quadratic fields; genus theory / ambiguous classes
ideas.usually_credited_to: Gauss (genus theory), classical algebraic number theory
ideas.where_published: Standard textbook fact (e.g. in treatments of genus theory)

ideas.what: Counterexample to triviality of the Galois action on Pic of the ring of integers, using a quadratic field with odd class number > 1.
ideas.modern_name: Nontrivial Galois action on class groups

deep.surprise_reason: A routine number-theory remark, offered as a counterexample in passing. Its only interest is biographical (the 'ask Serre' marginal note) and the context of Galois actions in the 1965 motive notes.
transcription_corrections: The first line most likely reads 'Ce n'est pas en général le cas, même si K_0 = Q'.
The struck-out word before 'des entiers de L' is a deleted false start. The phrase reads 'A étant l'anneau des entiers de L'.
'par symétrie' should be understood as the action x ↦ -x, i.e. inversion in additive notation; the reading seems correct.
The margin note reads 'demander à Serre ?'.
